purpose: Independent interleaved format comparison with native transition-boundary diagnostics
scope: Six direct WebRTC trials on one Linux x64 runner with identical producer/browser image digests, in 1s/3s/3s/1s/1s/3s order. No tunnel, TURN, MediaMTX, authentication or physical camera is exercised.

All six trials pass original media, playback, source-format and source-target recovery gates. The complete series has five passes and one failure: trial four misses exact first-presentation measurement because its first callback reports two submitted frames. The original failed verdict and null exact startup durations remain unchanged.

All twelve native-counter brackets (capacity and recovery) are valid. Counters remain unchanged from the post-boundary native snapshot to the final ordinary sample of each phase. This is diagnostic evidence; these trials do not use the later integrated boundary acceptance method or collect regular native-statistic timestamps.

The legacy sampled-counter method also observes no steady freeze in these trials. These measurements do not retrospectively reclassify the earlier failed matrices or prove an external host-scheduling cause.

Both down-holds recover all format ladders. Initial transition freeze durations overlap; public down-hold remains three seconds. Timing/CPU data concern these synthetic sources and this runner, not target hardware.

Browser callbacks are not guaranteed for every composed frame. The missing exact-first observation is distinct from failed playback; a conservative visible-frame measurement requires new visibility evidence rather than backfilling this trial.
